changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`

- names `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Both marketplace chunks were held by CHUNK CO-TENANCY, not by any import of the page: rolldown had parked `components/SuggestedBindingsPanel.tsx` (statically imported by the eager `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) in the first, and `console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx` (bare-imported by the package barrel for its SDUI registration) in the second. An `app-shell-eager-leaves` group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` isolates those co-tenants so the three declared-lazy pages chunk by their own dynamic-only reachability. The console eager closure moves 3180.2 KB → 3171.5 KB gzipped (−8,888 bytes, 48 → 45 eager chunks) with the three per-chunk ceilings unmoved.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `a8c550938` (merge-base with origin/main): 5 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1782 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2388 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36656110728)

| **Eager closure** (gzip, 330 chunks) | **3114.7 KB** | 3149.4 KB |
| Main entry chunk (gzip) | 149.5 KB | 350 KB |

| Status | **PASS** | — |

The **eager closure** is every chunk the entry reaches through static imports — what the browser fetches and parses before the app renders. The entry chunk on its own is a small fraction of it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c262d51ee30b2bc40bfe37d8546490e7516ec0ac`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11153 (body and its three comments: triage `5900733958`, claim `5901850933`, dev report `5902396944`), PR #11164 (body, 6-file list, the net diff against `main`), the head's check-runs (`filter=latest`), and head/base reads of the two touched sources plus `nav-selection.ts`, `useMetadata.ts`, `index.ts` and `package.json` for context. The binding direction is triage `5900733958`.

Check-runs on the head (`filter=latest`, read after the last one completed at 2026-09-30T01:52:28Z): 43 in all, 40 success, 3 skipped (dependabot and the two coverage jobs, which do not run on a PR head), 0 failed, 0 in progress. Green on the head: Type Check, Lint, Test (the 8 shards, dist pins, and the rollup), Build & E2E, Bundle Analysis, Spec Main Shape Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Changeset Declaration / Bump Policy / Fixed Group / Overwrite Report / Claim Re-read, Line Citation Gate, Control Byte Scan, Inert vi.mock Specifier Check, Pre-Install Import Graph Check, Docs Route Eager Closure Check and the doc/skill checks. The 12 runs still in progress when this review started (the test shards, Lint, Type Check, Spec Main Shape Gate) were waited for in the foreground; none was judged before it completed.

### ① Derived judgments

**The shared hook — right.** `useNavSelDeepLink` (`metadata-admin/useNavSelDeepLink.ts`, 117 lines) is the ONE deep link for both designers: `ResourceEditPage.tsx` drops its two effects and the five `nav-selection.js` imports (net -16 lines) and calls the hook; `InterfacesPillar` drops its two effects and `useSearchParams` and calls the hook. It is internal: `index.ts` at the head does not name it, `nav-selection.ts` at the head still exports only its parse/format/lookup helpers and imports nothing from React or the router, and `package.json` publishes only `.`. "Beside the helpers" is met by a sibling file; the stated reason (keeping `nav-selection.ts` React-free for `artifactStudioPath.ts`) is sound.

**The mirror's wait — right.** The mirror effect keeps its base keying (`[enabled, selection]`, i.e. the old `[navSel]` and `[type, selection]`) and adds one guard: `if (linkKey and not settled and appliedRef is not linkKey) return`. So the mount pass, which runs with no selection, no longer deletes `sel` while a parsed param is unapplied and `settled` is false. `settled = loaded and readOnly !== undefined`: the direction asked for "the tree has loaded"; the dev added "the write state has settled", which the read-only clause forces (below). Once the apply selects the item, the selection change re-runs the mirror, which writes the param back from the selection. Traced the flip-to-settled commit: the apply effect is declared before the mirror, so if a selection reset lands in that same commit the apply's `setNavSel`/`setSelection` still follows and the mirror's second pass restores the param.

**The once-only apply — right.** `appliedRef` is keyed on `scope + param` (`scope` is the item `name` on the editor page, empty on the pillar, as at base). The mirror's own write produces the same param, so the apply does not re-fire; a later selection change that rewrites `sel` to another id re-applies on that id, which is base behaviour. `draft` in the apply's deps means a pulse re-read (same app, `appStatus` stays `ready`) re-runs the effect but the ref stops it. `onApply` is read through a ref, so the non-memoized callbacks the two callers pass do not re-run it.

**The pillar's `loaded` — right.** `loaded: appStatus === 'ready'`, and the app-load effect calls `setAppDraft(body)` and `setAppStatus('ready')` in the same async continuation, so the `navTree` memo and `loaded` flip in one commit; the apply sees the loaded tree. `navDoc` is memoized on `navTree`, so the apply's `draft` dep does not churn per render.

**The Studio surface's tri-state `pkgWritable` — right, and nothing else changes behaviour.** At the head the state has exactly two readers besides its setters: `const readOnly = pkgWritable === false` (`:830`, unchanged) and the new `readOnlySettled={pkgWritable !== undefined}` (`:1290`). `readOnly` is `false` for `undefined` and for `null` alike, so every existing path (`!readOnly` on the rail toggle, the publish buttons, the object grid/form, the nav autosave `blocked`) reads the same as at base, where the value was `null` in both the in-flight and the failed case. What `null` means now is "asked and could not find out" (the catch sets it, where at base the catch left the initial `null`; the list-miss `?? null` is unchanged): for `readOnly` that is still "ungated", the surface's documented contract ("Unknown writability stays ungated; the server gate remains the authority"). Only the deep link tells the two apart, via `readOnlySettled ? readOnly : undefined`. So a package the list cannot answer for (`null`) settles as writable for the link and opens editing, consistent with the toggle being on offer there; a package still being asked for (`undefined`) holds the link. That is the right reading of the direction's "applying the link reads `readOnly`": it reads the same `readOnly` the toggle reads, once that value exists. `readOnlySettled` is an optional prop with default `true` on a component `index.ts` does not export; CI Type Check is green, so no caller broke.

**`ResourceEditPage` waiting on `useMetadataTypes` — right.** `readOnly = !canWrite && !createMode`, and `canWriteByType` is decided by `entry` from `useMetadataTypes` (`allowOrgOverride` / `allowRuntimeCreate`). Its `loading` starts `true` and flips once per client, so `readOnly: typesLoading ? undefined : readOnly` holds the link until `entry` exists; `loaded: !loading` uses the page's own draft-load flag (starts `!createMode`, cleared after `layered` and `getDraft` both return, on the error path too). The lock half of `canWrite` (`layered.editable`) lands in the same batch as `loading = false`. Cost: one destructured field and one ternary.

**Read-only selection, editor page — inside the direction and visible.** The `if (!editing) setSelection(null)` effect is keyed on `[editing]`, so a selection made while editing stays off is not cleared; the inspector branch renders `AppNavInspector` with `readOnly={formReadOnly}`. The pin asserts the inspector opens on the linked item with Label disabled, no "Add nav item", `sel` kept. The base comment claiming a read-only selection "is meaningless" was wrong and is gone with the block.

**Read-only selection, pillar — inside the direction as written, with a residual gap for ③.** Every `navSel` reader at the head is gated on `editNav` (`hasInspectorTarget`, `inspectorBodyEl`, the two `isSourcePage` terms, the canvas under `editNav`), so on a read-only package the held selection is inert and unrendered; the URL keeps `sel`, so the link stays shareable to a writable colleague. The direction's words are "selects the item without entering editing" and its reason is the blocked autosave; both hold. Rendering the selection would touch `NavTree` (objectui#11158, serial behind this card) or the rail inspector body, which the dispatch forbade. Note for the record: the pillar's read-only pin is observationally the same as its unknown-id control (no editing, param kept); that the apply actually reaches `onApply` there is shown by ablation 1, where forcing `enterEditing: true` turns exactly the three read-only pins red.

**Unknown id keeps the param — right.** The apply finds no hit and records nothing; the mirror, keyed on the selection, does not run again, so the URL stays as it was and no state moves. That is the literal "changes nothing". The base's deletion of the param at mount was the defect, not the control's expected outcome; the mirror still rewrites `sel` on the next selection change. Pinned on both designers, writable and read-only (4 of the 10 pins).

**The pins.** Ten pins in two files against the three the direction names: writable opens editing on the linked item after the draft loads and the URL keeps the param (pillar, editor); read-only selects without editing (pillar: no editing, no inspector value, param kept; editor: inspector open read-only, param kept); unknown id changes nothing (both designers, both write states). Plus two whole-surface pins that mount the real `StudioDesignSurface` with `fetchPackages` resolved by hand after the tree loads: a `writable:false` answer never enters editing, and the writable control opens the link only after the answer. The pillar pins mount the real `InterfacesPillar` under a `MemoryRouter`; the editor pins mount the real page with the registered `AppPreview` and `AppNavInspector`; only the metadata client is a double. Before-fix reds (pillar 6/6, twin 4/4, with the failure texts quoted in the report) are the dev's measurement and consistent with the mechanism: the writable pins on the missing Done toggle / inspector, every URL half on `expected null to be 'nav:nav_landing'`. The three ablations match their expected shapes: 1 (no read-only gate) exactly the 3 read-only pins red; 2 (unknown read as writable) exactly the 2 surface race pins red; 3 (wait line deleted) all 10 red, the base defect. Restores confirmed by blob and empty `git diff HEAD`.

**Surface.** Six files: the hook, the two named sources, two pin files, one changeset. No `NavTree`, no `navSurface.ts`, no `nav-selection.ts` edit. Two commits; the second only loosens the twin pin's `layered` double type.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` — confirmed. The PR body carries `Clause-②: no`; the claim's "why no" holds against the diff: the `?sel=nav:ID` shape, `DESIGNER_SEL_PARAM`, and every `nav-selection.ts` export are unchanged; nothing is added to `index.ts`; `useNavSelDeepLink` and `readOnlySettled` are reachable only by relative import inside `src/`, which `package.json` (`exports: "."`) does not publish; `pkgWritable` is component state. `StudioDesignSurfaceProps`, the one exported type from the file, is untouched. An internal prop and an internal hook publish nothing, so the changeset `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` (`.changeset/11153-nav-deep-link-survives-mount.md`) matches what the diff publishes: a behaviour fix. Changeset Declaration, Bump Policy, Fixed Group, Overwrite Report and Claim Re-read are green on the head. The pending `6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md` flag is a report-only note about the `SuggestedBindingsPanel` import, which this diff does not touch.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (six), each answered:
1. **Widening inside `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`: the tri-state probe and the `appStatus` move — forced and minimal.** The direction requires the link to read `readOnly`; the dev measured that the surface's write state can be unknown when the tree arrives (its package-list request is not ordered against the pillar's two-round-trip app load), and ablation 2 shows the link then enters editing on a package that answers read-only, the very class the direction bars. The change is the smallest that distinguishes the states: initial and reset value `undefined`, `null` set in the catch, one prop line, no other reader touched. The `appStatus` `useState` moves up because the hook call now reads it; the hooks stay unconditional.
2. **`ResourceEditPage` reads `typesLoading` — forced by the same clause, minimal** (judged in ①).
3. **The hook is a sibling file, not re-exported from `nav-selection.ts` — right;** the direction's "beside the helpers" is met and the module stays React-free.
4. **Unknown id keeps the param — right** (judged in ①).
5. **Commit trailers use the repo's model-free pair.** Not a contract matter; noted.
6. **Worktree removed after the PR opened.** Housekeeping; noted.

`open_questions`: none declared; none found.

Out-of-scope note (a) — **real at the head, pre-existing, and left the same by this PR.** At the head the rail's Edit toggle renders under `appStatus === 'ready' && !readOnly` (`:2505`) with `readOnly = pkgWritable === false`, which is `false` while the list is in flight; its own `onClick` is the only writer that turns `editNav` off (`setEditNav` has two call sites: the toggle and the hook's `onApply`, which only sets `true`); the nav autosave is `blocked: ... || readOnly` (`:2058`). So Edit clicked in the window, followed by `writable:false`, hides the toggle and leaves the canvas open with saves blocked. At base the same three lines exist with `pkgWritable` initially `null`, so it is pre-existing.
